subject: OpenAI GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna, released 2026-09-22
central_claim: GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are a publishable AI engineering topic because OpenAI primary sources support a bounded E2/R1 claim: the release lowers the API price tier for GPT-6 reasoning models and, more importantly for long-running agents, pairs those models with prompt caching, explicit cache breakpoints, reasoning-effort updates that preserve cached prefixes, stable tool-list guidance and cache diagnostics. The article does not claim independent proof that Sol or Luna is generally superior to competing models.
conflicts: OpenAI develops and sells GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna and the API services described in the cited documents.
No vendor briefing, account, credit, hardware, sponsorship, advertising relationship, NDA or embargo was used.

selection.reason: The topic directly affects software teams evaluating reasoning models for Codex-style coding agents and long-running business agents. It is new in the current discovery window, supported by multiple OpenAI primary documents, and useful because the engineering decision is not merely model ranking but prompt-cache-aware request design, tool stability and observability.

claims.claim: GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna change the practical economics of long-running agents by combining lower GPT-6 model prices with prompt-cache-aware controls and diagnostics; integration teams should evaluate cache prefix stability, tool-list management, reasoning effort changes and cache miss observability before treating the models as a simple price cut.

claim_source_ledger.claim: OpenAI released GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna on 2026-09-22 and documents API model IDs `gpt-6-sol` and `gpt-6-luna`.
claim_source_ledger.version: OpenAI API changelog, September 22, 2026 GPT-6 Sol/Luna entry
claim_source_ledger.method: Opened the official OpenAI API changelog and cross-checked the launch post availability section.
limitations: No live API request was sent to test account-level availability.
OpenAI is the model developer and source of the release note.
conflict_of_interest: OpenAI develops and sells the cited models.

claim_source_ledger.claim: The API changelog lists standard per-1M-token prices for prompts up to 272K input tokens: GPT-6 Sol at $2 input, $0.20 cached input and $10 output; GPT-6 Luna at $0.10 input, $0.01 cached input and $0.50 output.
claim_source_ledger.version: OpenAI API changelog, September 22, 2026 pricing entry
claim_source_ledger.method: Read the Sol/Luna changelog pricing bullets and compared them with the launch post pricing table.
limitations: The changelog notes that longer prompts, cache writes and processing tiers require pricing details outside the short entry.

claim_source_ledger.claim: OpenAI says GPT-6 prompt caching reuses eligible shared prefixes within a 30-minute window and offers discounts of up to 90% on cached input tokens.
claim_source_ledger.version: Better prompt caching for GPT-6, published 2026-09-22
claim_source_ledger.method: Opened OpenAI's prompt caching announcement and checked it against the prompt caching API guide.
limitations: Actual cache hit rates depend on request shape, model routing, tool definitions and workload.
No application trace or billing record was inspected.
conflict_of_interest: OpenAI operates the caching system and sells cached-input processing.

claim_source_ledger.claim: The prompt caching guide documents explicit cache breakpoints and says supported GPT-6 and later models can change reasoning effort by appending a `configuration_update` item while preserving the earlier cached prefix.
claim_source_ledger.version: OpenAI API prompt caching guide, accessed 2026-09-25
claim_source_ledger.method: Read the explicit breakpoint section and the change-reasoning-effort section of the prompt caching guide.
limitations: No request was executed to validate the cache-preservation behavior.
Compatibility limits may differ by model and API state.

claim_source_ledger.claim: The prompt caching guide tells developers to keep tool definitions, ordering and schemas stable, use `tool_choice: none` rather than removing tools, and use `allowed_tools` to restrict callable tools while preserving the supplied tool list.
claim_source_ledger.version: OpenAI API prompt caching guide, manage tools with append-only updates
claim_source_ledger.method: Read the manage-tools guidance in the prompt caching guide.
limitations: The newsroom did not measure the magnitude of cache savings from these practices.
Tooling behavior can vary with application design.
conflict_of_interest: OpenAI defines the API behavior being described.

claim_source_ledger.claim: Prompt cache diagnostics can return `cache_hit`, `cache_miss`, `comparison_response_not_found` or `unavailable`; cache miss results can include a reason such as `tools_changed` and missed-token estimates, but usage fields remain the billing measurement.
claim_source_ledger.version: OpenAI API prompt cache diagnostics guide, accessed 2026-09-25
claim_source_ledger.method: Read the diagnostics examples, response interpretation table and token-count caveat.
limitations: Diagnostic estimates may differ from actual usage accounting.

claim_source_ledger.claim: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra system card change log says a GPT-6 Sol/Luna appendix was added on 2026-09-22; the appendix treats Sol and Luna as High capability in Cybersecurity and Biological/Chemical domains, and below High in AI Self-Improvement.
claim_source_ledger.version: GPT-6 Astra System Card, September 22, 2026 change log and GPT-6 Sol/Luna appendix
claim_source_ledger.method: Opened the Deployment Safety Hub system card, read the change log and the GPT-6 Sol/Luna appendix.
limitations: OpenAI is the system-card author and evaluated its own models.
No independent audit or reproduction was used for this claim.
conflict_of_interest: OpenAI develops and deploys the evaluated models.
